state.context:
Defeater register of Circuit OS (backend/validation/defeaters.py). A defeater is a recorded doubt about a claim; a claim that cites an open defeater is reported as defeasible.
D1. Doubt: predict() is validated against mathematics and ngspice, not hardware. Applies to: every closed-form or simulated claim about circuit behaviour. Eliminated by: a bench measurement agreeing within tolerance.
D2. Doubt: the MCU is represented by simplified electrical models (a resistive supply load sized from its run current, and a Thevenin GPIO pin), not the device. Applies to: claims whose scope.model names an MCU model. Eliminated by: reachset conformance against the real device.
D3. Doubt: no external engineer has read a generated explanation cold. Applies to: the explanation layer. Eliminated by: criterion 12's review.
D4. Doubt: coverage growth cost may outrun one engineer. Applies to: the generator library as a whole. Eliminated by: measured authoring cost per generator.
D5. Doubt: an LLM may write the IntentIR, so the specification is untrusted. Applies to: designs whose IntentIR provenance is llm and whose properties nobody has signed. Eliminated by: a person signing the back-translated properties.
D6. Doubt: block proofs may not compose into board claims. Applies to: any design built from more than one generator. Eliminated by: interface contracts, first tested when two generators share a rail.
D7. Doubt: datasheet parameters feeding predict() and the rule tables are unverified. Applies to: claims that read ratings, forward voltages or pin tables. Eliminated by: provenance per parameter.
D8. Doubt: pi is irrational, so a z3 encoding of a cutoff frequency must bracket it. Applies to: z3-proved claims involving pi or another transcendental. Eliminated by: rational bracketing in the proof compiler.
D9. Doubt: a generator bug makes predict() confidently wrong and nothing catches it. Applies to: every generator not yet under the M1 mutation matrix. Eliminated by: the M1 matrix detecting seeded faults in that generator's output.

state.context:
How Circuit OS grades a claim (backend/validation/claims.py). A claim's grade is derived from its checking method through one table; it is never typed per claim.
proof_checked (the proof was checked by a proof checker) -> G0
z3_unsat (z3 finds no counterexample over the declared box) -> G1
monotone_corners (exact when monotone in every argument; the corners are evaluated) -> G1
closed_form (an exact formula at the declared nominal scope) -> G1
exact_graph_check (exhaustive over the design as written) -> G1
sound_enclosure (interval arithmetic enclosing every possible value) -> G2
certificate -> G3
bounded_model_check (all states explored up to a bound) -> G4
ngspice_nominal (one ngspice simulation at nominal values) -> G5
sampled (random samples of the parameter space) -> G6
asserted (stated; no check was run) -> G7
A rule that was not assessed on a design is shown as a critical row graded G7.

state.context:
Circuit OS retry policy for producing the IntentIR from a prompt (amendment X5; backend/ai/intent_producer.py).
- API error (the model provider fails: outage, overload, authentication or rate-limit error): do not retry; return HTTP 503.
- Schema failure (the forced tool_use input does not validate against the IntentIR schema): do not retry; return HTTP 422 carrying the raw tool input.
- Semantic refusal (the input is valid but no generator's envelope() accepts it): retry once; the retry may add a value it failed to record the first time, but may never change or drop a value the user asked for.
- A request genuinely outside the catalogue (none of the five generators could ever cover it) is refused, not negotiated: no retry.

state.context:
Circuit OS patch rules (amendments X2 and X4; backend/api/routes/patch.py, backend/ai/intent_patcher.py).
- A patch is an RFC 6902 operation list over IntentIR.requirements. It edits the requirement, never the circuit: a path into CircuitIR (components, nets, values) is rejected.
- Every operation written by the LLM patcher must cite, verbatim, words from the user's command, and those words must contain the value written. An uncited operation is rejected.
- A patch submitted against a version other than the design's current version is rejected with 409 version_conflict.
- A patch whose operations leave the requirements unchanged is not a new version: it returns the same design unchanged.
- Otherwise the patched requirement is re-derived through the same envelope() -> generate() -> predict() gate and accepted as the next revision.
- Patches are never retried.

state.context:
Circuit OS critical rules (CLAUDE.md), never to be violated:
one_rule: LLM output -> JSON -> IR schema -> deterministic compilers. The LLM never writes SPICE, KiCad or firmware directly.
celery: simulation always runs via Celery, never inline in an HTTP handler.
mcu_resistor: the MCU SPICE model is a resistor (100 ohm on the Uno), never a voltage source.
columnar_output: ngspice batch output is columnar; the regex v(x) = y does not match it.
kicanvas_ssr: kicanvas is loaded with a dynamic import and ssr: false; it is never server-rendered.
postgres: all designs persist to PostgreSQL; no in-memory design_store = {}.
cors_first: CORS middleware is added before any route is registered.
static_bom: BOM pricing is static; no live Digikey/LCSC API calls.
